narrative.overview: Since 2026-10-30 the whole site lives in the evening: every section sits on forest green, deep green or a full-bleed photograph, never on a light page. White carries the words, the logos and the one action to take; a pale jade picks out eyebrows, icons and links. The owner's brief: a "green and white combination everywhere", with the whole viewport covered by green, images or video. The tone is quiet luxury, not glamour. Big real photographs carry the emotion and glow against the dark; the type is a classical serif at one weight beside a plain sans; ornament is limited to a white hairline divider with a small diamond. Density is generous on marketing pages and tighter on hotel pages, where facts (sizes, beds, check-in) sit in tidy two-column lists. Rejected on purpose (owner decisions): the pastel white-and-green look, the ivory "emerald & gold" look (2026-10-25 to 10-30), the arched "temple window" cards, and photo walls that mix several hotels together.
keyCharacteristics: Forest green everywhere, with deep and raised green bands for rhythm; no light sections.
White text, white logos (all-white copies of the client artwork) and white primary buttons with green text.
Pale jade for small accents only.
Cormorant Garamond 600 for every heading, Inter for everything else.
Photography first: full-bleed hero slideshow, large editorial photos, photo marquees.
Contact is always visible: white "Call to Book" in the header, sticky mobile bar, booking card.

rules.name: The No Light Page Rule
rules.body: Every section background is forest, raised, deep or a photo. Never ivory, white or grey.

rules.name: The White Means Go Rule
rules.body: A solid white fill is the primary action. Don't use white fills for cards, badges or backgrounds.

rules.name: The WhatsApp Is Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal belongs to WhatsApp (and the "Coming soon" badge). A call is white, a chat is teal, everywhere.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Cormorant is loaded at 600 only. Make hierarchy with size, case and italic, never with a second serif weight.

rules.name: The Lining Numerals Rule
rules.body: Serif numbers are lining (`lining-nums`), because Cormorant's default old-style figures make phone numbers look uneven.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Only an element that overlaps or follows the page (pill, sticky card, menu) gets Lift. Ordinary content cards stay flat with a gold hairline.

dos: Do keep every section on forest, raised or deep green, or on a full-bleed photo or video.
Do use white for text, logos and the primary button; pale jade for eyebrows, icons and links.
Do use the all-white logo files (`*-white.webp`, made by `scripts/build_white_logos.py`) anywhere a logo sits on green.
Do put the white divider under every section headline and a jade eyebrow above it.
Do keep headings in Cormorant Garamond 600 with lining numerals, and everything else in Inter.
Do give every moving thing a Pause control and a still version for reduced motion.
Do label any 3D render "Artist's impression" on the image.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px and check new colour pairs against WCAG AA.
donts: Don't bring back light sections (ivory, white or grey backgrounds), the gold accents, the pastel look or the arched hotel cards.
Don't put a border on the header.
Don't mix photos from different hotels in one wall or strip.
Don't use white hairlines above 35% opacity; they turn into stripes on dark green.
Don't add a second serif weight, a third typeface or decorative script.
Don't add heavy shadows, gradients on buttons or glossy effects; depth comes from the green levels, photos and hairlines.
Don't use teal for anything that isn't WhatsApp or a status badge.
